rounds.text: Jindal Photo Ltd carries significant fundamental deterioration, evidenced by a trailing twelve months compounded profit growth of -127% [E18] and a net profit drop of 75% year-on-year [E62]. The operating margin trajectory is troubling, having dropped to -506% in the TTM from 98% three years prior, marking a steep 604 percentage point decline alongside a four-year yearly trend of decreasing margins [E26, E28]. Profitability metrics universally lag, with ROE at -2.23% [E8], ROCE at -1.34% [E9], and a low median ROE of -2% over the last year [E25]. Technical and institutional participation signals are similarly weak, with the stock trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E44], carrying negative institutional money flow [E41], and sitting alongside a crushing historical worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -95.9% [E47]. Borrowings have also ticked upward to Rs 65 Cr against Rs 59 Cr a year earlier [E36], accompanied by a low interest coverage ratio warning [E55]. Conceded: the company maintains a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.06x [E34], solid short-term liquidity with a current ratio of 2.68x [E35], and a robust 102% compounded sales growth over five years [E14].

While the bear points to a TTM compounded profit growth of -127% [E18] and a 75% YoY net profit drop [E62], quarterly evidence shows immediate operational recovery with operating margin rebounding to 98% in June 2026 against 83% in the year-ago quarter (+15 percentage points) [E27]. Conceded: the yearly operating margin trend is decreasing [E28] and TTM margins dropped [E26], but this masks powerful structural sales acceleration, including a 102% compounded sales growth over 5 years [E14] and a massive 744% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months [E16]. The bear highlights rising borrowings at Rs 65 Cr [E36] and low interest coverage [E55], yet the company remains almost debt free with a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.06x [E34, E53] and comfortable short-term liquidity featuring a 2.68x current ratio [E35]. Furthermore, fears regarding profitability ignore a robust 5-year median return on equity of 17% [E23] and positive cash generation, delivering Rs 7 Cr in both operating and free cash flow as of March 2026 [E31, E32]. Finally, while the stock trades below its moving averages [E44] and suffers from institutional outflow [E41, E64], it sits in a powerful Financial Services tailwind with a score of +1.00 [E67] and is attractively priced at 1.05x book value relative to the sector benchmark of 1.33x [E6].
